brief: Turaev, The Yang–Baxter equation and invariants of links (Invent. Math. 92, 527–553, 1988) — enhanced Yang–Baxter operators give link invariants via braid closure; the HOMFLY (P) and Kauffman (F) polynomials arise this way, with state models.
extended:
**The Yang–Baxter equation and invariants of links** — V. G. Turaev. Inventiones mathematicae 92, 527–553 (1988).

§2 recalls Yang–Baxter operators R on V⊗V (V free of rank m over a commutative ring K) and introduces enhanced YB-operators (EYB): a quadruple S = (R, μ, α, β) of a YB-operator R, an endomorphism μ of V and invertible scalars α, β satisfying the compatibility conditions needed for Markov invariance. §3 attaches to each EYB-operator S an isotopy invariant T_S of links, computed on a braid presentation as the trace of the braid's image composed with μ^{⊗n}, normalised by α and β so that it is invariant under both Markov moves; T_S is annihilated by the characteristic polynomial of R (Theorem 3.2.1). §4 studies special EYB-operators (from the R-matrices of the fundamental vector representations for the series A^(1), and B^(1), C^(1), D^(1), A^(2)) and shows the resulting invariants are equivalent to the two-variable polynomials P (HOMFLY) and F (Kauffman). §5 gives a state model for T_S under restrictions on S, and §6 a non-oriented version used to prove Theorem 4.3.4.

**Why it may bear here.** The direct braid-closure route from an R-matrix to a link invariant, with no von Neumann or Hecke algebra in between (the paper says so). A companion to wenzl1988 in the same volume. No bib entry existed before this ingest.
